newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares mixed, seen fluctuating.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares mixed, seen fluctuating.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Friday and traders said they expected prices to fluctuate until more news about President Boris Yeltsin's heart operations emerges.
"The market returned into an absolutely calm condition, where changes are measured by a few percent," said Alexei Goncharov, head of information department at Russian Brokerage House.
"This state will last as long as the president is being prepared for the operation," he said.

Andrei Galperin, a trader from Creditanstalt-Grant, said the market had also benefited from news that Russia's bank creditors had committed most of Russia's Soviet-era debt to the London Club which is eligible for rescheduling.
"The market became livelier in the evening when the Russian debt news appeared," he said. "It is good news, some orders appeared after that."
Goncharov said Russian operators showed most interest in power utilities, Rostelekom and LUKoil, as these most liquid shares fell sharply at the beginning of the week.
Prices nosedived at the beginning of the week after the surgeon likely to operate on Yeltsin said the operation could be delayed or called off altogether.
Gazprom was traded at $0.341 after $0.345 at Thursday's close, Irkutskenergo fell to $0.093 from $0.095, Mosenergo was at $0.867 after $0.869 and LUKoil was steady at $9.05.
